Name: Rule30Research
Description: Research provenance and dependency-aware assessments. Human-readable proofs remain imported assertions, not formal certificates.

Assertions.Description: Every claim in the ledger: definitions, theorems, finite verifications, hypotheses and falsified attempts.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: Role of the claim in the research: Definition, Theorem, Known result, Finite check, Hypothesis, Bridge obligation or Prize problem.

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The Effortless loop that added this claim; empty for claims carried over from research v05.

schema.name: StatusGroup
schema.Description: Proved (definition, proved or rederived known), Checked (finite verification only), Falsified, Superseded or Open.

schema.name: PremiseCount
schema.Description: Direct premises this claim depends on.

schema.name: DependentCount
schema.Description: Claims that list this one as a direct premise.

schema.name: EvidenceCount
schema.Description: Evidence files linked to this claim.

schema.name: RevisionCount
schema.Description: Recorded status changes of this claim.

schema.name: DescendantCount
schema.Description: Claims that rest on this one, directly or transitively.

schema.name: Predicate
schema.Description: The modeled predicate this claim is about, if any.

schema.name: PredicateVerdict
schema.Description: The model's verdict on the predicate's bounded instances.

schema.name: PredicateIsFinitelyDecidable
schema.Description: 1 when the model can decide the full statement.

schema.name: IsModelLinked
schema.Description: 1 when the claim is tied to a modeled predicate.

schema.name: PredicateIsRefuted
schema.Description: 1 when a counterexample instance fails in the model.

schema.name: PredicateIsVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the model decides the statement true.

schema.name: EffectiveStatus
schema.Description: The status the ledger uses: FALSIFIED when the model holds a counterexample, FINITE_VERIFIED when the model decides an open or checked claim true, otherwise the reported status.

schema.name: IsModelDecided
schema.Description: 1 when the model, not a report, decides the status.

schema.name: IsModelContradicted
schema.Description: 1 when the report asserts the claim (proved, checked or definitional) and the model refutes it: the report is wrong. An OPEN claim the model refutes is decided, not contradicted.

schema.name: ModelVerdict
schema.Description: The model's verdict on the claim's predicate; NOT MODELED for a claim stated only in words.

schema.name: IsCached
schema.Description: 1 when the *Cache fields of this row hold the last fresh compile (filled by loop_tools.build, cleared by every save).

schema.name: IsModelLinkedCache
schema.Description: Cached IsModelLinked from the last fresh compile; read by IsModelLinked while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: ModelVerdictCache
schema.Description: Cached ModelVerdict from the last fresh compile; read by ModelVerdict while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: EffectiveStatusCache
schema.Description: Cached EffectiveStatus from the last fresh compile; read by EffectiveStatus while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsModelDecidedCache
schema.Description: Cached IsModelDecided from the last fresh compile; read by IsModelDecided while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsModelContradictedCache
schema.Description: Cached IsModelContradicted from the last fresh compile; read by IsModelContradicted while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: StatusGroupCache
schema.Description: Cached StatusGroup from the last fresh compile; read by StatusGroup while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsUsableCache
schema.Description: Cached IsUsable from the last fresh compile; read by IsUsable while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: IsProofEligibleCache
schema.Description: Cached IsProofEligible from the last fresh compile; read by IsProofEligible while IsCached = 1.

schema.name: OnCurrentPath
schema.Description: 1 when the claim is a step of the plan in force.

schema.name: LoopTargetCount
schema.Description: Loops (planned, running or done) linked to this claim.

data.Name: B3

data.Statement: The center has limiting frequency one-half.
data.Name: P2

data.Statement: The official computational-effort conjecture, once model and quantifiers are fixed.
data.Name: P3

data.Statement: For k>=3 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}): if q_k(P/2)=1 then the least period of the forcing word q_k=y_{k-1} OR y_{k-2} is exactly P.
data.Name: TF

data.Statement: If j>=1 and eps_j=1 (least period of y_j is twice that of its forcing word) then y_j(P_j/2)=1.
data.Name: TG

data.Statement: For k>=3, if some parent j in {k-1,k-2} attains P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}) and has eps_j=1, then Q_k=P.
data.Name: TH

data.Statement: For all k>=3 the least period of the forcing word equals max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}); no OR of two parent diagonals ever has a period smaller than both.
data.Name: H7

data.Statement: If H7 holds for all k>=3 then the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (H7 implies H4).
data.Name: TI

data.Statement: Exact least diagonal periods, forcing periods and parities certified through offset 64 (largest period 2^27) by an independent big-integer implementation that reproduces all 52 v05 period-word hashes and agrees with a direct lattice evolution for t<=4096.
data.Name: F5

data.Statement: Every diagonal is 1 at its half period: y_j(P_j/2)=1 for all j>=1 (would close the open case of H7 through TF at t=0).
data.Name: H14

data.Statement: Cascade lemma: for k>=4 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), if y_j(P/2)=1 for some 2<=j<=k-1 then Q_k=P.
data.Name: TJ

data.Statement: For every k>=3, Q_k=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), and the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (induction on k using TJ, TG, TA).
data.Name: TK

data.Statement: For every k>=3, P_k = P_{k-1}*(1+eps_k): the least period repeats or doubles, never otherwise; and it doubles infinitely often.
data.Name: TL

data.Statement: For k>=4, if eps_{k-1}=1 then eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 (doubling at k decided by the parity of the grandparent diagonal).
data.Name: H15

data.Statement: eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 for every k>=4, with no doubling assumption on k-1.
data.Name: H16

data.Statement: After a doubling at k-1 (k>=4), eps_k equals the parity of the number of ones of y_{k-2} over its least period.
data.Name: TM

data.Statement: For k>=5 the least diagonal period never doubles three times in a row; hence log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3).
data.Name: TN

data.Statement: Finite discrepancy: |2 S(N) - N| <= 3 sqrt(N) for all 16 <= N <= 2^20, S(N) the number of ones among c(0..N-1).
data.Name: H9

data.Statement: Finite run bound: every maximal constant center run [T,V] with 1 <= T and V < 2^20 - 1 has length <= 2 log2(T+1) + 4.
data.Name: H13

data.Statement: For every period 1 <= p <= 2^17 and every onset T <= 917498, some t >= T has c(t) != c(t+p) (2^20 center bits; independent reproduction of E2).
data.Name: F6

data.Statement: Every plateau of the doubling sequence (maximal run of eps_k=0, k>=3) has length at most 7.
data.Name: H18

data.Statement: If every plateau has length at most L, then log2 P_k >= 2 + floor((k-3)/(L+1)) for all k>=3; a plateau bound forces exponential growth of the diagonal periods.
data.Name: TP

data.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 72 (largest period 2^31); all 64 E10 period-word hashes reproduced; new diagonals agree with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
data.Name: F7

data.Statement: For k>=3: if eps_k=1 the diagonal has an even number of ones per period; if eps_k=0 that parity equals the parity of the number of ones of q_k at odd positions.
data.Name: TO

data.Statement: eps_k is a function of (eps_{k-1}, eps_{k-2}, o_{k-1}, o_{k-2}) for every k>=5, where o_j is the parity of the number of ones of y_j per period.
data.Name: H19

data.Statement: The center is eventually p-periodic iff some agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) is infinite; so a finite bound on agreement runs for every p implies P1.
data.Name: TQ

data.Statement: On the first 2^20 center bits, every agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) for 1<=p<=4096 has length at most 44.
data.Name: H21

data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k(t)=x(-t+k,t) is eventually periodic, with least eventual period a power of two dividing 2^k.
data.Name: TR

data.Statement: Exact least eventual periods and onsets of the left-edge diagonals certified for k<=72 (largest period 2^3, latest onset 100); agrees with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
data.Name: F8

data.Statement: The left edge grows at most half as fast as the right: log2(left-edge period of w_k) <= log2(P_k)/2 for every k>=1.
data.Name: H22

data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k has least eventual period at most 8.
data.Name: H23

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=600; reproduces loop 9 for k<=72 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
data.Name: F9

data.Statement: The left-edge front moves at 5/4: |onset_k/k - 5/4| <= 0.02 for every 1000 <= k <= 5000.
data.Name: H24

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=5000; reproduces loop 10 for k<=600 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
data.Name: F10

data.Statement: Some left-edge diagonal with k < 20000 has least eventual period 32.
data.Name: H25

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=19999; for every 20<=k<=19999 the onset exceeds k, so the center c(t)=w_t(t) is read before its left-edge diagonal settles.
data.Name: F11

data.Statement: If the center p-agrees at t and t+1 then column -1 p-agrees at t when c(t)=1, and column -1 p-agrees at t iff column 1 does when c(t)=0: under center agreement, column -1 is column 1 read at the center's zero-times.
data.Name: TS

data.Statement: For every onset 1<=T<=10 and every nonconstant primitive word a of period p<=4, the left cone and the inverse rule alone exclude a p-periodic center of word a from onset T: no column-1 window is compatible once L reaches some L<=4T+4p+8.
data.Name: H26

data.Statement: Left-cone relaxation table for every onset T<=10 and every primitive word of period <=4: the number of column-1 windows (on the zero-times) compatible with a periodic center and the single-seed cone, for L<=4T+4p+8, with the first L that has none; the true (c,r) windows pass the same checker.
data.Name: F12

data.Statement: For every onset T, every p>=2 and every nonconstant word a of least period p, the left-cone relaxation (periodic center word a from T, free column 1, inverse rule, cone of T0) is unsatisfiable at some finite L(T,a).
data.Name: B5

data.Statement: For L>=T the left-cone relaxation is in bijection with rows R at time T on positions -T+1..-1 such that the Rule 30 evolution of the left half from R, with the center prescribed as boundary x(0,t)=c'(t), satisfies x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at every one-time t<=T+L-1; column 1 is determined, and count(T,a,L)<=2^(T-1).
data.Name: TU

data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word a of period p<=6 and every onset 2<=T<=T_max(a) that exact enumeration completes (live-set cap 2^23), the left cone excludes the periodic center with L(T,a)<=4T+4p+8.
data.Name: H27

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths L(T,a) of the left-cone relaxation for every primitive word of period <=6, onsets from 2 up to the enumeration limit per word (largest completed onset 144); vectorised search validated against the loop 13 table and an independent SAT encoding of TU.
data.Name: F13

data.Statement: For t>=T and j<=t-T, x(-1,t) = x(-j-1,t-j) XOR XOR_{i=1..j}(x(-i,t-i) OR x(-i+1,t-i)); in the relaxation the leading term is a free row bit for t<=2T-2, the edge for t=2T-1 and 0 for t>=2T, so every one-time constraint from time 2T on is a parity of ORs along a light ray with no free-row term.
data.Name: TV

data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word of period 7 or 8 and every onset T>=8 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^23), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64: the relaxation dies by time 2T+64, independently of T.
data.Name: H28

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths, death times and violated cone cells of the left-cone relaxation for all 366 primitive words of periods 7 and 8 at onsets [8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192] up to the enumeration limit (largest completed 192); death-cell histograms recorded.
data.Name: F14

data.Statement: For the single-zero words a=0 1^(p-1), p in [8, 10, 12, 16], and every onset T>=32 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^25), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64.
data.Name: H29

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths, excess and death cells of the left-cone relaxation for the single-zero words of periods [8, 10, 12, 16] at onsets from 32 to the enumeration limit (largest completed 384), with the excess fitted against T and log2 T.
data.Name: F15

data.Statement: In the forward form, the one-time constraints at T<=t<=2T-2 fix the row bit at position -(t-T+1) as a function of the bits to its right and leave the bits at zero-time positions free: exactly 2^Z rows survive to 2T-2 (Z = zero-times in [T,2T-2]), and every constraint at t>=2T-1 is a Boolean function of those Z bits.
data.Name: TW

data.Statement: For every T>=2 and every nonconstant periodic word, each of the 2^Z rows of TW violates x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at some one-time t>=2T-1.
data.Name: B6

data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period p<=5 and every onset 4<=T<=18, the largest algebraic degree over the Z free bits among the one-time constraints applied before death is at least Z-1: the kill is maximally nonlinear, so B6 is not linear algebra over GF(2).
data.Name: H30

data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period <=5 and onset 4..18: Z, the TW count check, and for each one-time constraint after 2T-2 until death its algebraic degree over the Z free bits, live counts before and after, and whether it was constant on the live set.
data.Name: F16

data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, a cone cell violated by every surviving window exists at the death step, and its time t*(T) is non-decreasing in T with steps 0 or 1.
data.Name: H31

data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 at onsets 4..46: the death window, survivors, the violated cone cells with counts, the common killing cells, whether the edge cell is among them, and t*(T).
data.Name: F17

data.Statement: B6 for the period-2 words 01 and 10: for every onset T>=2, each TW row for a 2-periodic center violates a one-time constraint at or after 2T-1 (equivalently, the Rule 30 center is not eventually 2-periodic).
data.Name: B7

data.Statement: B6 for every nonconstant word of least period p>=3.
data.Name: B8

data.Statement: The dyadic wall is exact for period 2 past onset 36: for a=01 and every onset 47<=T<=50 the left-cone relaxation dies at window exactly 64, and for a=10 at exactly 65.
data.Name: H32

data.Statement: L(T) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 2<=T<=50 (loop 18 data plus onsets 2, 3 and 47..50 computed here with cap 2^26), with survivors at the death step.
data.Name: F18

data.Statement: The 64-wall is exactly the TW boundary phenomenon: for the words 011,101,110 (pinned window 66) and 0111,1011,1101,1110 (pinned window 64) the death window keeps its pinned value from the first pinned onset through T=63 and exceeds it at T=64,65,66; for 01 and 10 at onsets 51 and 52 it stays at 64 and 65.
data.Name: H33

data.Statement: Structure of the 64-wall for the word 01 at onsets 37..46: forced cells on the death ray (none in the cone interior), tie classes by column (columns 1-3 tied, 4-5 partly, 6 onward untied), GF(2) independence of the 33 one-time functions over all rows for T<=18; and the L(T) table of H33 for period-3 and period-4 words at onsets 44..66.
data.Name: F19

data.Statement: With every settled left-edge diagonal imposed on the periodic-center relaxation (exact values, or periodicity only), the death window exceeds the settled frontier by at most 8 (exact) or 16 (periodic only) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 8<=T<=160 the search completes: the clash with the settled zone is local.
data.Name: H34

data.Statement: Settled-zone relaxation table for the words 01 and 10, exact and periodicity-only modes, onsets 8..160: frontier, death window, excess, peak live set, failing columns; the true lattice satisfies every imposed constraint to time 400.
data.Name: F20

data.Statement: The left half x(i,t), i<=-1, is a function of c(0..t-1) and the seed, and whenever c(t)=1 the forward rule forces c(t+1)=NOT x(-1,t): the center is left-consistent.
data.Name: TX

data.Statement: No left-consistent sequence (c(0)=1, and c(t+1)=NOT x(-1,t) whenever c(t)=1, with x the left half it generates from the seed) ends in a periodic tail with a nonconstant word.
data.Name: B9

data.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, every left-consistent prefix c(0..T-1) is killed by the 2-periodic tail before time 2T-1, inside the zone where the free-row relaxation provably cannot kill (TW).
data.Name: H35

data.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period 3 or 4 and every onset 4<=T<=32, every left-consistent prefix is killed by the periodic tail before time 2T-1.
data.Name: H36

data.Statement: Seeded relaxation table: for the words 01, 10 (onsets 4..46) and every primitive word of period 3 and 4 (onsets 4..32), the number of left-consistent prefixes, survivors, and the largest and mean death excess t*-T with its histogram; tree growth ratio 1.4981 per step.
data.Name: F21

data.Statement: For some E>=12, the near-center windows (c(t), x(-1..-E,t)) shown by left-consistent sequences at t=45 miss at least half of the 2^(E+1) possible windows.
data.Name: H37

data.Statement: There is an E<=30 such that every width-(E+1) near-center window shown by a left-consistent sequence at any time 19<=t<=45 dies within E-1 steps under the tail 01 and under the tail 10 (the finite part K(E) of B9 for period 2).
data.Name: H38

data.Statement: Near-center window language of left-consistent sequences for E=4..30 (even) and t=19..45: language sizes, stability in t (E<=22), the smallest missing windows, and the windows surviving E-1 steps under each period-2 tail.
data.Name: F22

data.Statement: H39: on the real prefix, left-consistency kills every nonconstant primitive tail a with |a| <= 3, spliced on at any onset 1 <= T <= 10, within 3|a| steps of the onset.
data.Name: H39

data.Statement: Let A be the least set of width-25 near-center windows (c(t), x(-1..-24,t)) that contains every window shown by a left-consistent prefix at t=19 and is closed under one step of the left half (outer bit free, next center bit forced by TX after a 1). For each period-2 tail, every window in A fails one of the next 24 one-time checks. H40 implies B9 for period 2 at every onset.
data.Name: H40

data.Statement: For every E >= 1, the width-(E+1) window step with the outer cell free (center NOT x(-1) after a 1, free after a 0) reaches every window from every window in at most 2E+1 steps; so the closure of any nonempty window set is all 2^(E+1) windows. A free outer cell never gives an invariant, at any width.
data.Name: TY

data.Statement: For every time 19 <= t <= 160 and each tail 01, 10, every width-25 near-center window shown at t by a left-consistent prefix fails one of the next 24 one-time checks (H38 at E=24 extended from t <= 45 to t <= 160).
data.Name: H41

data.Statement: Merged left-consistent states for t = 0..160: the number of distinct rows, the distinct width-25 windows (t >= 19), the windows among the loop 25 survivors, and the longest survival of a state under each period-2 tail (up to 120 checks).
data.Name: F23

Dependencies.Description: Declared one-step logical dependencies between assertions.

schema.name: Conclusion
schema.Description: The assertion that depends on the premise.

schema.name: Premise
schema.Description: The assertion the conclusion relies on.

Prerequisites.Description: Transitive closure of Dependencies, one row per (conclusion, ancestor), regenerated by research/loop_tools.py.

schema.name: ConclusionKey
schema.Description: The assessment this transitive premise feeds.

schema.name: Premise
schema.Description: A transitive ancestor of the conclusion (including itself).

schema.name: IsSelf
schema.Description: 1 for the row pairing a claim with itself.

schema.name: IsBlockingAncestor
schema.Description: 1 when this ancestor is not usable and so blocks the conclusion.

Assessments.Description: Compiled status of each assertion given the status of all its ancestors.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: The claim being assessed, in words.

schema.name: StatusGroup
schema.Description: Proved, Checked, Falsified, Superseded or Open, from the reported status.

schema.name: SelfUsable
schema.Description: 1 when the claim itself is usable as a premise.

schema.name: CurrentStatus
schema.Description: BLOCKED when an ancestor is not usable, otherwise the effective status.

schema.name: SupportCount
schema.Description: Number of evidence files linked to this assertion.

schema.name: EvidenceGap
schema.Description: 1 for a reported finite verification with no evidence file; a model-decided one is its own evidence.

schema.name: AncestorBlockedCount
schema.Description: Ancestors (not counting the claim itself) that are not usable.

schema.name: IsAtRisk
schema.Description: 1 when a claim reported as established rests on an ancestor that is open, falsified or superseded. Should always be 0.

schema.name: AncestorCount
schema.Description: Claims this one rests on, directly or transitively.

schema.name: ProjectKey
schema.Description: Dashboard this assessment rolls up to.

schema.name: EffectiveStatus
schema.Description: The status the ledger uses (model-decided where it can be).

schema.name: IsModelDecided
schema.Description: 1 when the model decides the status.

data.Statement: Cascade lemma: for k>=4 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), if y_j(P/2)=1 for some 2<=j<=k-1 then Q_k=P.

data.Name: TK

data.Name: H15

data.Name: H16

data.Name: TM

data.Name: TN
data.Statement: For k>=5 the least diagonal period never doubles three times in a row; hence log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3).

data.Name: H9
data.Statement: Finite discrepancy: |2 S(N) - N| <= 3 sqrt(N) for all 16 <= N <= 2^20, S(N) the number of ones among c(0..N-1).

data.Name: H13

data.Name: TP

data.Name: F7

data.Name: TO

data.Name: H19

data.Name: TR

data.Name: F8

data.Name: TS
data.Statement: If the center p-agrees at t and t+1 then column -1 p-agrees at t when c(t)=1, and column -1 p-agrees at t iff column 1 does when c(t)=0: under center agreement, column -1 is column 1 read at the center's zero-times.

data.Headline: P1 waits on two open obligations, B7 (period 2) and B8 (period 3 and up), at the bottom of a chain of proved reductions. No prize problem is closer to proved; the open obligations are sharper.
data.Approach: Go after period 2 first, through B9: no left-consistent sequence ends in a 2-periodic tail. TX makes the center left-consistent, so B9 is exactly what B1 needs, and it is weaker than B5. Finite checks are strong: every left-consistent start at onsets 20 to 46 dies within 22 steps of a period-2 tail (F21), and every near-center window of width 25 that such sequences produce at times 19 to 45 dies within 23 steps (H38).
data.Missing: A uniform description of the reachable windows that still kills. Freeing the outer cell at each step reaches every window and lets 18,432 survive (H40). Tying the outer cell to the settled left-edge zone does not help for long: the settled zone starts about 0.27 t columns out (17 at t = 64, 35 at t = 128), so column 24 is settled only until about t = 85, and the unsettled band between the window and the settled zone widens without bound.
data.NextHypothesis: Does the finite kill hold past t = 45? Merge left-consistent prefixes by their row (their future depends only on it) and test every reachable state from t = 19 to t = 160 against both period-2 tails (H41). Prove that a free outer cell floods the window closure at every width (TY), which rules out widening the window without a run.
data.Estimate: Proving P1 itself: well under 1 percent, unchanged. Proving the period-2 case on this route: lowered to about 1 in 20, because the window idea needs information from a band that widens with t. Loop 26 is designed to settle whether the route is viable at all.

data.Headline: P1 waits on two open obligations, B7 (period 2) and B8 (period 3 and up), at the bottom of a chain of proved reductions. Loop 26 closed the near-center window route to period 2; the attack moves to whole rows.
data.Approach: Go after period 2 first, through B9: no left-consistent sequence ends in a 2-periodic tail. TX makes the center left-consistent, so B9 is exactly what B1 needs. Prefixes with the same row have the same future, so merged by row they are few: 4.6 million states at t = 160 against an extrapolated 10^28 prefixes, and every one dies under both period-2 tails (F23). A proof needs a description of the reachable rows that is closed under the step and contains only rows that die.
data.Missing: A finite description of whole reachable rows. Near-center windows cannot be it: a free outer cell floods any window closure (TY), and the kill time of real states grows with t (46 and 47 checks by t = 111, H41), so no fixed-width window kills. The far left of a row is where the settled diagonals make it periodic, so an automaton reading the row from the left edge inward may stay small.
data.NextHypothesis: Read each reachable row from the left edge inward and build the smallest automaton accepting exactly the reachable rows at each t. If its size stops growing in t through t = 160, a regular invariant is plausible and the next step is to close it under the step and check that every row it accepts dies. If it keeps growing like the state count, no regular description exists at this level and the route through B9 needs another idea.
data.Estimate: Proving P1 itself: well under 1 percent, unchanged. Proving the period-2 case through B9: about 1 in 30, lowered because the window route closed and the kill time grows with t. Loop 27 gives a decisive reading on the whole-row route.

Operators.Description: The symbols formal statements are built from: binders (quantifiers, limits), connectives, relations, arithmetic and the functions of the model (c, x, rule30, cTail, ...).

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: binder, infix, prefix, apply, atom, var or const: how a term with this operator is written out.

schema.name: Arity
schema.Description: Number of arguments (a binder has two: its condition and its body).

schema.name: IsModeled
schema.Description: 1 when the model computes this operator (a table or field gives it its value); 0 when it is only a named symbol so far.

Terms.Description: One node of a formal statement: an operator with its argument terms, a variable, or a constant. A binder holds its bound variable, its condition (Arg1) and its body (Arg2). The text, the quantifier count and whether a quantifier ranges over an infinite domain are computed from the tree.

schema.name: TermOperator
schema.Description: The operator (var and const for leaves).

schema.name: Variable
schema.Description: The variable of a var leaf, or the variable a binder binds.

schema.name: Constant
schema.Description: The value of a const leaf.

schema.name: BoundsVariable
schema.Description: On a binder: 1 when its condition gives the variable a finite range (as in Theorem C's t in [T, 2T + p]).

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The model-native loop that added this term; empty for the core predicates.

schema.name: PredicateKey
schema.Description: The predicate whose statement this node belongs to (a plain key, not a reference: Predicates already points at the root term).

schema.name: OpKind
schema.Description: How the term is written out.

schema.name: OpIsModeled
schema.Description: 1 when the model computes the operator.

schema.name: VarUnbounded
schema.Description: 1 when the variable ranges over an infinite domain.

schema.name: Rendered
schema.Description: The term written out in Wolfram Language style, computed from the tree.

schema.name: IsUnboundedBinder
schema.Description: 1 for a quantifier over an infinite domain.

schema.name: IsUnmodeledOperator
schema.Description: 1 when the model does not compute this operator yet.

Predicates.Description: The properties stated about the model: definitions, theorems, bridge obligations and the three prize problems. The formal statement is a Terms tree; its bounded instances are computed from the model; a model-native loop adds its hypotheses here as rows.

schema.name: Problem
schema.Description: Definition, Known result, Theorem, Bridge obligation, Hypothesis, or the prize problem it is (P1, P2, P3).

schema.name: InstanceKind
schema.Description: Which reference of PredicateInstances decides an instance.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: A gloss in words; the formal content is the term tree.

schema.name: FailureRefutes
schema.Description: 1 when a failing instance is a counterexample to the statement; 0 when it only means the horizon did not decide it.

schema.name: BoundSlope
schema.Description: For bound hypotheses: the bound is slope * |a| + intercept.

schema.name: DomainMin
schema.Description: For bound hypotheses: the smallest index (N, T) the statement covers.

schema.name: CoversDomain
schema.Description: 1 when the instance rows enumerate the whole bounded domain of the statement, so holding on all of them verifies it; 0 when they are a sample (a model horizon shorter than the statement).

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The model-native loop that stated this predicate; empty for the core predicates.

schema.name: Formal
schema.Description: The formal statement, written out from its term tree.

schema.name: UnmodeledOperatorCount
schema.Description: Operators of the statement the model does not compute yet.

schema.name: IsComputable
schema.Description: 1 when every operator of the statement has a meaning in the model.

schema.name: IsFinitelyDecidable
schema.Description: 1 when the model can decide the full statement, not only bounded instances.

schema.name: RowCount
schema.Description: Instance rows, in or out of the domain.

schema.name: InstanceCount
schema.Description: Bounded instances in the domain of the statement.

schema.name: IsRefuted
schema.Description: 1 when a counterexample instance fails: the statement is false.

schema.name: IsVerified
schema.Description: 1 when the statement is finite, its instances cover its domain and every one holds: the model decides it true.

schema.name: FiniteVerdict
schema.Description: What the model says about the bounded instances.
schema.formula: =IF({{IsCached}}=1,{{FiniteVerdictCache}},IF({{InstanceCount}}=0,"NO INSTANCES",IF({{FailingCount}}=0,"HOLDS ON EVERY INSTANCE",IF({{FailureRefutes}}=1,CONCAT("REFUTED BY ",{{FailingCount}}," OF ",{{InstanceCount}}," INSTANCES"),CONCAT({{FailingCount}}," OF ",{{InstanceCount}}," UNDECIDED AT THE HORIZON")))))

schema.name: IsCached
schema.Description: 1 when the *Cache fields of this row hold the last fresh compile (filled by loop_tools.build, cleared by every save).

data.Statement: The prize setup: a single black cell at position 0 at time 0, then Rule 30 at every cell and time.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per run: the run is Rule 30 from the single seed.
data.Name: pr-d0-setup

data.Statement: Rule 30's table is Wolfram's polynomial (equivalently left XOR (center OR right)).
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per transition of rule 30.
data.Name: pr-rule30-polynomial
data.Formal: ForAll[l, True, ForAll[q, True, ForAll[r, True, (rule30[l, q, r] == Mod[(((l + q) + r) + (q * r)), 2])]]]

data.Statement: From the single seed under a quiescent rule, every cell outside the light cone is white.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per run: the run satisfies the conditions that make the cone exact.
data.Name: pr-light-cone

data.Statement: Problem 1: the center column is not eventually periodic.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per period p <= 24: every candidate (p, T) with T <= (depth - p)/2 has a witness t >= T with c(t + p) != c(t) inside the horizon (the witnesses are PeriodicityCandidates.FirstMismatchFrom).
data.Name: pr-p1-non-periodic
data.Formal: NotExists[p, (p >= 1), NotExists[T, (T >= 0), ForAll[t, (t >= T), (c[(t + p)] == c[t])]]]

data.Statement: The center column is not eventually constant (the period-1 case of Problem 1).
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance: every onset T <= (depth - 1)/2 has a witness t >= T with c(t + 1) != c(t).
data.Name: pr-k1-not-constant

data.Statement: Theorem C: for every T and p, column 0 or column 1 has x(i, t) != x(i, t + p) for some t in [T, 2T + p].
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per period p: every window (T, p) that ends inside the horizon holds (the windows are MismatchWindows rows).
data.Name: pr-tc-mismatch-window

data.Statement: Theorem D: a black center run starting at T ends by 2T+1, a white one by 4T+5.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per center cell: the cell lies within the bound of the run it belongs to.
data.Name: pr-td-run-bounds

data.Statement: TX: whenever c(t) = 1 the rule forces c(t + 1) = NOT x(-1, t), and the left half depends only on the center's past: the center is left-consistent.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per time step t < depth of the real center.
data.Name: pr-tx-left-consistent

data.Statement: B9 on the real prefix: the real center up to T followed by a a a ... (a nonconstant, primitive) is not left-consistent: some one-time t has cTail(t + 1) != NOT xTail(-1, t). B9 and TX imply it; B1 follows from it.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per tail candidate (word, onset): left-consistency kills it inside the horizon (onset + 12).
data.Name: pr-b9-tail-killed
data.Formal: ForAll[a, (Nonconstant[a] && (LeastPeriod[a] == Length[a])), ForAll[T, (T >= 1), Exists[t, (t >= (T - 1)), ((cTail[a, T, t] == 1) && (cTail[a, T, (t + 1)] != (1 - xTail[a, T, -1, t])))]]]

data.Statement: Problem 2: each color occurs on average equally often in the center column.
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per tolerance epsilon: the density of the whole computed prefix is within epsilon of 1/2.
data.Name: pr-p2-equal-frequency

data.Statement: Problem 3: no admissible machine computes c(n) with effort O(n) (the displayed predicate; the prose says "at least O(n)").
data.InstanceMeaning: One instance per algorithm: an admissible algorithm's effort ratio still grows at the horizon.
data.Name: pr-p3-effort
data.Formal: NotExists[m, !StoresAnswer[m], (ForAll[n, (n >= 1), (Output[m, n] == c[n])] && (Limsup[n, (n -> Infinity), (Effort[m, n] / n)] < Infinity))]
